svg.title: A gap buffer: the gap goes to the cursor once, and then each key fills one byte of it

g.title: The file is opened: its 12 bytes at the start of a block of 28, and the gap, 16 bytes of room, after them. The cursor is at byte 4.
An edit at byte 4, and the gap is at 12: first the gap moves there. The 8 bytes between, "cat sat\n", cross from before the gap to after it: moved 8, 8 in all.
Then f goes into the gap's first byte, and the gap is a byte shorter: 15.
Key a at byte 5: the gap is there already. The key goes into it, the gap is a byte shorter (14), and nothing moves: moved 0.
Two more keys, t and a space: each goes into the gap, which gets a byte shorter each time, and nothing else moves. "fat " is typed: 8 bytes moved in all, every one of them for the first key.
An edit at byte 15, and the gap is at 8: first the gap moves there. The 7 bytes between, "cat sat", cross from after the gap to before it: moved 7, 15 in all.
Then ! goes into the gap's first byte, and the gap is a byte shorter: 11.
Backspace: the byte before the cursor, "!", is erased. The gap first steps back over it (1 byte moved), then simply widens to take it in: the gap is 12 again. Six edits, 16 bytes moved in all.
g.text: the erased byte is now part of the gap
